spec.title: LLM Spend History
spec.description: Spend, requests and tokens by day and week over week, from totals that recording rules copy out of the traces every 10 minutes: Claude Platform, OpenRouter, and crok's own reports for Codex, GLM and DeepSeek. Starts on the day the rules were installed. Opens on the last 14 days, as long as Grafana Cloud's free tier keeps metrics.

panels.title: Spend
panels.description: Claude (estimated at list prices) plus OpenRouter (billed) plus what crok reported. codex, glm and deepseek are crok's own reports (crok's cost per call: the provider's when it reports one, else the standard API price); codex is every OpenAI call crok makes. Recorded every 10 minutes for the window that ended 20 minutes earlier, so the newest 20-30 minutes are not in yet. History starts when the recording rules were installed. Days are UTC days.

panels.title: Claude, estimated
panels.description: Claude spend from tokens at list prices. Recorded every 10 minutes for the window that ended 20 minutes earlier, so the newest 20-30 minutes are not in yet. History starts when the recording rules were installed. Days are UTC days.

panels.title: OpenRouter, billed
panels.description: The cost OpenRouter reported. Recorded every 10 minutes for the window that ended 20 minutes earlier, so the newest 20-30 minutes are not in yet. History starts when the recording rules were installed. Days are UTC days.

panels.title: Codex, GLM, DeepSeek
panels.description: What crok reported for the providers without traces of their own. codex, glm and deepseek are crok's own reports (crok's cost per call: the provider's when it reports one, else the standard API price); codex is every OpenAI call crok makes. Recorded every 10 minutes for the window that ended 20 minutes earlier, so the newest 20-30 minutes are not in yet. History starts when the recording rules were installed. Days are UTC days.

panels.title: Requests
panels.description: Calls to every provider. Recorded every 10 minutes for the window that ended 20 minutes earlier, so the newest 20-30 minutes are not in yet. History starts when the recording rules were installed. Days are UTC days.

panels.title: Tokens
panels.description: Input plus output tokens. Recorded every 10 minutes for the window that ended 20 minutes earlier, so the newest 20-30 minutes are not in yet. History starts when the recording rules were installed. Days are UTC days.

panels.title: Error rate
panels.description: Failed calls divided by all calls, from the traces only: the usage APIs do not count failures. A call the user interrupted in crok is not a failure. Recorded every 10 minutes for the window that ended 20 minutes earlier, so the newest 20-30 minutes are not in yet. History starts when the recording rules were installed. Days are UTC days.

panels.title: Spend, week over week
panels.description: Spend in the last 7 days and how much more (or less, below zero) than the 7 days before. Last 7 days is the seven days up to the end of the time range; the 7 days before are the seven before that. Both come from the recorded history (LLM Spend History), which lags 20-30 minutes, and do not depend on the time range's length.

panels.title: Requests, week over week
panels.description: Calls in the last 7 days, compared with the 7 days before. Last 7 days is the seven days up to the end of the time range; the 7 days before are the seven before that. Both come from the recorded history (LLM Spend History), which lags 20-30 minutes, and do not depend on the time range's length.

panels.title: Tokens, week over week
panels.description: Input plus output tokens in the last 7 days, compared with the 7 days before. Last 7 days is the seven days up to the end of the time range; the 7 days before are the seven before that. Both come from the recorded history (LLM Spend History), which lags 20-30 minutes, and do not depend on the time range's length.

panels.title: Error rate, week over week
panels.description: Failed calls divided by all calls (a call the user interrupted in crok is not a failure). Last 7 days is the seven days up to the end of the time range; the 7 days before are the seven before that. Both come from the recorded history (LLM Spend History), which lags 20-30 minutes, and do not depend on the time range's length.

panels.title: Spend by provider, week over week
panels.description: Spend per provider in the last 7 days and the 7 before; Change is how much more (below zero: less). codex, glm and deepseek are crok's own reports (crok's cost per call: the provider's when it reports one, else the standard API price); codex is every OpenAI call crok makes. Last 7 days is the seven days up to the end of the time range; the 7 days before are the seven before that. Both come from the recorded history (LLM Spend History), which lags 20-30 minutes, and do not depend on the time range's length.

panels.title: Requests by provider, week over week

Both come from the recorded history (LLM Spend History), which lags 20-30 minutes, and do not depend on the time range's length.

panels.title: Tokens by provider, week over week
panels.description: Input plus output tokens per provider in the last 7 days and the 7 before. Last 7 days is the seven days up to the end of the time range; the 7 days before are the seven before that. Both come from the recorded history (LLM Spend History), which lags 20-30 minutes, and do not depend on the time range's length.

panels.title: Spend per day, and 7 days earlier
panels.description: Bars: spend in each UTC day. Dashed line: the same weekday a week earlier, so each day reads against last week's. Recorded history only (no backfill). Recorded every 10 minutes for the window that ended 20 minutes earlier, so the newest 20-30 minutes are not in yet. History starts when the recording rules were installed. Days are UTC days.

panels.title: Spend per day

The legend total is the spend over the range. codex, glm and deepseek are crok's own reports (crok's cost per call: the provider's when it reports one, else the standard API price); codex is every OpenAI call crok makes. Recorded every 10 minutes for the window that ended 20 minutes earlier, so the newest 20-30 minutes are not in yet. History starts when the recording rules were installed. Days are UTC days.
